digest.en: An FBI agent arrested an Energy Department employee for allegedly aiding Yemen's Houthis. Simultaneously, a Russian election fraud expert was beaten after the vote. Brazil's attorney general rejected Trump's funding plans as intolerable meddling.

articles.title: FBI arrests Energy Department employee on charge of trying to support Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen
articles.summary: Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, a 51-year-old employee at the United States Department of Energy in Richland, Washington, was arrested on October 1, 2026. Federal authorities charged him with attempting to support the Iran-backed Houthi movement in Yemen. The FBI executed the arrest on Thursday. Ellaboudy is scheduled to appear in court on Friday for his initial hearing. Court records indicate that no attorney is currently available to represent him or speak on his behalf regarding the case.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula says only he can stop rise of fascism under Bolsonaro’s son
articles.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva led a massive rally in Rio de Janeiro on Saturday. He declared himself the sole barrier against the return of far-right "fascists" to power. The event preceded Sunday’s presidential election, which observers view as the most consequential in decades. Lula, eighty years old, framed the vote as a decisive choice between his left-wing government and the political movement associated with former president Jair Bolsonaro.

articles.title: Flydubai Passenger Recounts Saving Stabbed Pilot
articles.summary: A Georgian-Israeli dentist on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel helped a pilot allegedly stabbed by his co-pilot on September 30. Shota Musayev left his wife to assist the injured crew member. He feared for his own survival during the incident. The flight was diverted to safety. Georgian-Israeli dentist Shota Musayev told RFE/RL that he feared he might not survive when he left his wife’s side to help after the lead pilot was allegedly stabbed by his co-pilot during a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel on September 30.

articles.title: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
articles.summary: The World Health Organization warned that delayed medical supplies to Gaza risk devastating consequences. Lifesaving medicines and prosthetics are stuck in transit from Israel. The UN agency appealed for a massive aid influx before winter arrives. Palestinians in the enclave urgently need these critical resources. Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

articles.title: Row erupts over Cairo mural depicting Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin
articles.summary: Cairo authorities removed a 66-metre mural from Tahrir Square before Xi Jinping’s state visit. The artwork depicted Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin. Critics alleged it revived Afrocentric claims about Pharaohs’ origins. The removal sparked a public row over historical representation. Artwork created in Tahrir Square for Chinese president’s state visit to Egypt is painted over amid allegations it revived Afrocentric claims about Pharaohs’ originsOn the eve of Chinese president Xi Jinping’s state visit to Cairo last month, the city authorities were busy removing a 66-metre-long mural from the esteemed guest’s line of sight. Depicting the Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti, t.

articles.title: After Russia's Elections, An Expert On Fraud Is Arrested And Reportedly Beaten
articles.summary: Russian security forces detained fraud analyst Aleksandr Kynev in Moscow after he warned of vote falsifications benefiting United Russia. He was reportedly beaten while in custody. The incident highlights a clash between security agencies and political operatives within the Kremlin. In the days between the elections and his arrest, Aleksandr Kynev had pointed to evidence of falsifications benefitting the United Russia party.

articles.title: US blast simulation targets China’s alleged secret nuke testing
articles.summary: The US Department of Energy conducted underground blast experiments in Nevada. These tests aim to detect clandestine nuclear detonations. The program addresses concerns about China's secret testing capabilities. Faced with rising great-power suspicions and the challenge of verifying clandestine, cavity-muffled detonations, the US is turning to high-precision subterranean blast experiments in the Nevada desert to strip covert nuclear testing of its technical cover.

articles.title: The Bolsonaros…they’re back! Brazil heads to the polls – podcast
articles.summary: Brazil held its first-round presidential election on Sunday. Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former president, ran to succeed his father. Jair Bolsonaro was convicted in September 2025 of attempting a coup. The campaign tested whether his political legacy survived the conviction. The Bolsonarosthey’re back! Brazil heads to the polls – podcast. The Bolsonarosthey’re back!

articles.summary: AI agents don’t go rogue. That’s something only humans do. Nevertheless, a New York Times article – representative of much news coverage of AI – described an OpenAI hacking as “A. I. bots going rogue and independently spearheading a cyberattack.” Name-brand artificial intelligence agents have been on a hacking spree in 2026. articles.title: Brazil attorney general says meddling ‘cannot be tolerated’ after Trump funding plans revealed
articles.summary: Jorge Messias calls Guardian report ‘an important alert for Brazilian sovereignty’ as nation prepares to go to pollsBrazil’s attorney general has said foreign meddling in his country’s institutions and democracy “cannot be tolerated” after a Guardian report revealed how the Trump administration was pushing to direct funds to a campaign against the Brazilian supreme court. Writing on X, Jorge Messia Brazil attorney general says meddling ‘cannot be tolerated’ after Trump funding plans revealed.

articles.title: Kyrgyz Activist Gets 2 Years For Criticizing Growing Chinese Presence
articles.summary: The Lenin District Court in Bishkek found activist and politician Mavlyan Askarbekov guilty and sentenced to two years in prison on offenses related to a law on incitement of racial, ethnic, national, religious, or interregional hatred, a verdict he called "absurd." Kyrgyz Activist Gets 2 Years For Criticizing Growing Chinese Presence.

articles.title: Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists
articles.summary: Exports of crude oil from the Middle East hit their highest level in September since the war with Iran began, reinforcing a trend of increased supplies despite Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, according to analysis of shipping and commodity market data by industry observers. Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists.

articles.title: Georgia Summons Iranian Ambassador Over Remarks On Revered Queen Ketevan
articles.summary: Georgia summoned Iran’s ambassador after his planned book Georgia has summoned Iran’s ambassador after his plans to publish a personal interpretation of Queen Ketevan’s history sparked criticism from ruling party lawmakers. Revered as a saint in Georgia, Ketevan was tortured and killed in Persia in the 17th century after refusing to renounce Christianity. Georgia Summons Iranian Ambassador Over Remarks On Revered Queen Ketevan.

articles.title: Tbilisi Rebukes Iranian Envoy Over Social Media Post On Canonized Georgian Queen
articles.summary: Iran’s ambassador to Georgia announced plans to publish research on Queen Ketevan, a 17th-century monarch executed by Persia and later canonized by the Georgian Orthodox Church. Tbilisi summoned the envoy over the move, which the Foreign Ministry viewed as an inappropriate intervention in Georgian religious history. The incident highlights ongoing diplomatic friction between the two nations. Georgia’s government rejected the ambassador’s framing of the historical figure.

articles.title: Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny
articles.summary: For years, Pakistan’s claim that the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan operates from sanctuaries inside Afghanistan produced a familiar exchange: Islamabad accused, Kabul denied, and each new militant attack triggered another round of recrimination. That pattern is becoming harder to sustain. The sanctuary dispute can now be tested against a growing body of evidence rather than competing claims [] The p Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny.

articles.title: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
articles.summary: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday. Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO.

articles.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
articles.summary: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province. Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp.

articles.title: 'Exhausted' Afghan Refugees Get Extension At Camp In Qatar As US Lawmakers Urge Action
articles.summary: Qatar will keep the Afghan refugee camp open for another nine months after the closure deadline passed, according to Afghan refugees being held at a camp in Qatar have been told it will be kept open for another nine months after a deadline for its closure passed, but they face continuing uncertainty over their fate amid an ongoing bar on entry to the United States.

articles.title: Daredevil Jaan Roose completes slackline walk high above central Seoul
articles.summary: Estonian slackliner Jaan Roose walked a 160-metre line 120 metres above Seoul on Thursday. The ribbon stretched between the Koreana hotel and Dong-A Media Center near Gyeongbokgung palace. He completed the first of two planned attempts. Estonian completed first of two attempts to navigate narrow ribbon, 160 metres long and 120 metres high, near the city’s famous Gyeongbokgung palace on ThursdayThe lunchtime crowds drifted slowly back to their offices along central Seoul’s main boulevard, heads up and phones raised to the sky. High above, a narrow ribbon ran between the Koreana hotel and the Dong-A Media Center, a few hundred metre.

articles.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad
articles.summary: Support for white Afrikaners, anti-communism and others reveals how US redefining what qualifies as human rightsWith hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a massive $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner.

articles.title: South African leader urges men to speak up on gender-based violence after series of killings
articles.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa urged men to take responsibility for gender-based violence. He announced new measures following a recent wave of murders. Authorities face anger over inadequate protection for women. President announces measures amid anger at authorities over recent murders of womenSouth Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders. Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women.

articles.title: MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities
articles.summary: Institutions have for years turned to China for funding opportunities but national security concerns are mountingMI5 issues spy alert to UK universities over Chinese front company stealing researchThe security alert issued by MI5 regarding a Chinese state-owned conglomerate accused of conducting espionage in the UK reveals the extent to which British intelligence remains concerned about Beijing’s MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities.

articles.title: Burundi agrees to receive ‘third-country’ migrant deportees from US
articles.summary: Burundi joins several other African nations in accepting people deported under Trump’s hardline policyBurundi has agreed to join a clutch of ⁠other African nations in receiving migrants from other countries deported from the US under ⁠Donald Trump’s hardline ⁠immigration ​policy. However, the authorities in Bujumbura, the country’s economic capital, said Burundi will only accept those not accused o Burundi agrees to receive ‘third-country’ migrant deportees from US.

articles.title: Palestinians yearn for ‘a return to normal life’, says top Middle East peace envoy
articles.summary: Acting UN Special Coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov said Palestinians in Gaza yearn for a return to normal life as the UN pushes to restore utilities and rebuild infrastructure amid severe access restrictions. The effort faces obstacles from damaged roads The UN is continuing efforts to support Palestinians in Gaza amid major challenges to humanitarian access, reconstruction and the restoration of essential services, according to Ramiz Alakbarov, Acting UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process.

articles.title: AI tool that copied actor’s ‘lustrous’ voice violated his rights, Tokyo court rules
articles.summary: A Tokyo court ruled an AI tool violated actor Kenjiro Tsuda’s rights. The TikTok account cloned his voice for generated videos. The verdict grants human voices legal protection under Japanese publicity law. Kenjiro Tsuda wins case against TikTok account in landmark Japanese verdict to protect publicity rightsA court in Japan has ruled that the human voice has legal protection after a landmark case involving a well-known actor and a TikTok account that he claimed had cloned his “lustrous” baritone voice in its AI-generated videos. Tokyo district court said on Wednesday that voices should enjoy the same.

articles.summary: भारत ने पहलगाम हमले के बाद सिंधु जल समझौता रोक दिया है। पाकिस्तान को चेनाब-ब्यास लिंक टनल से डर है। डेटा शेयरिंग बंद होने से पाकिस्तान कानूनी अड़ंगे नहीं लगा पा रहा। पहलगाम आतंकी हमले के बाद भारत ने सिंधु जल समझौता रोक दिया है. इससे पाकिस्तान में हाहाकार मचा हुआ है लेकिन इस्लामाबाद की नींद 8.7 किलोमीटर लंबी 'चेनाब-ब्यास लिंक' टनल प्रोजेक्ट ने भी उड़ा रखी है.

articles.summary: गांधी जयंती पर दिल्ली के जंतर मंतर से मुंबई के शिवाजी पार्क तक विपक्ष ने चुनाव आयोग के खिलाफ प्रदर्शन किया। कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी ने लाखों लोगों के जुटने का दावा किया, जहां राहुल गांधी और अखिलेश यादव ने भी भाग लिया। दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर से लेकर मुंबई के शिवाजी पार्क तक गांधी जयंती के मौके पर चुनाव आयोग के खिलाफ कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी और विपक्ष ने जबरदस्त प्रदर्शन शुरू कर दिया है.

articles.title: भारत के इस ‘हथियार’ ने अमेरिका में मचाया हड़कंप, पहले अटैक में ऐसी तबाही, पैनिक में धड़ाधड़ लगाए फोन
articles.summary: पूर्व अमेरिकी खुफिया अधिकारी ने बताया कि भारत के मिशन शक्ति में अंतरिक्ष में लाइव सैटेलाइट को नष्ट करने से अमेरिका में हड़कंप मचा था। इस घटना के बाद अमेरिकी अधिकारी घबराहट में दिल्ली को फोन करने लगे थे। भारत के 'मिशन शक्ति' को लेकर एक बार फिर बातें होने लगी हैं. एक पॉडकास्ट के दौरान पूर्व अमेरिकी खुफिया अधिकारी ने बताया है कि इस मिशन में इस्तेमाल हुए एक हथियार को देखकर अमेरिका में किस तरह पैनिक मच गया था.
